b481248658.q: What is the Net Investment Income Tax and when was it introduced under the Affordable Care Act?
b481248658.a: The Net Investment Income Tax, also known as the Obamacare Medicare surtax, is a 3.8% tax on net investment income that was instituted as part of the Affordable Care Act in 2013. It was initially believed that revenue from this tax would fund Medicare, but the final bill was changed so that revenue goes into the general fund instead. The tax is calculated on Form 8960 and applies as a surtax above and beyond the regular tax rate.

1ecd89fb01.q: What income thresholds trigger the Net Investment Income Tax for individual and married filers?
1ecd89fb01.a: The Net Investment Income Tax applies only if income exceeds certain thresholds: $250,000 for married filing jointly or $200,000 for single individuals and head of household filers. These thresholds are based on modified adjusted gross income and are not indexed to inflation, meaning more taxpayers are being pulled into the tax annually as incomes rise over time.

3a1ecfe85b.q: What is the tax savings for a business owner who correctly backs out active business income from Form 8960?
3a1ecfe85b.a: In the example provided, a business owner with $350,000 in wages, $50,000 in interest and dividend income, $300,000 in business income, and $3 million from a business sale would owe $127,300 in Net Investment Income Tax if prepared incorrectly. When business income and capital gains are correctly backed out on lines 4B and 5B of Form 8960, the tax drops to just $1,900, resulting in savings of over $125,000.

10a4fc9207.q: Why is the Net Investment Income Tax mistake commonly missed on business owners' tax returns?
10a4fc9207.a: The mistake occurs frequently because tax software does not automatically back out active business income and requires manual adjustments on Form 8960. Tax preparers working during busy tax season may overlook it, particularly if they do not have direct communication with clients or lack details about business sales. Most taxpayers are unfamiliar with Form 8960 and its mechanics, making it difficult to catch the error when reviewing their own returns.

66430b28af.q: Which specific lines on Form 8960 should business owners review to ensure active business income is excluded?
66430b28af.a: Business owners should examine lines 4B and 5B on Form 8960. If these lines are blank, it likely means that active business income and capital gains have not been properly backed out of the Net Investment Income Tax calculation. Comparing the form to examples of correctly and incorrectly prepared versions can help identify whether business income has been properly excluded.
